kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: generic, produced by multiple Chinese manufacturers; no single branded OEM confirmed for the ELEGOO-bundled unit
generic_equivalents: 35BYJ series (larger frame, different mounting, not a drop-in swap)
identity.package: module, permanent-magnet geared can motor with a 5-wire pigtail and connector

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small motor that turns in fixed, precise steps instead of spinning freely, so a microcontroller can command an exact rotation and know where the shaft ended up without any extra position sensor.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Precise positioning tasks such as camera pan/tilt rigs, clock hands, valve actuators, and small mechanisms that need to move a known amount and hold position.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Four internal coils are energized in sequence, and each energizing step pulls a geared magnetic rotor forward by a small fixed angle. A built-in gearbox (about 64:1) turns many small internal steps into one much finer, stronger step at the output shaft.

pinout.name: Orange
pinout.notes: one end of coil A; other end shares the common Red wire

pinout.name: Red
pinout.notes: center-tap wire shared by all four coils; connects to the driver board's '+' terminal

pins.pin_1_identification: The motor ends in a small white 5-pin plastic plug that only fits the matching driver board socket one way. Genuine 28BYJ-48 pigtails use this wire order: Orange, Pink, Yellow, Blue, Red (common).

electrical.operating_voltage: 5V DC (this kit's variant; a visually identical 12V-coil version also exists and is not interchangeable)
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: no formal absolute-maximum figure is published by the generic manufacturers of this part; treat 5V as the ceiling for this variant
electrical.typical_current: 0.1 A (100 mA) per energized coil, per the Botland retailer's spec sheet
electrical.max_current: not confirmed from a source I could fetch; some tutorials cite roughly 240 mA total when two coils are active in full-step drive mode, but this could not be traced to a source that loaded
electrical.logic_level: the motor itself is not driven by logic-level signals directly; it is driven at 5V through the ULN2003 driver board
electrical.interface: digital, only through the ULN2003 driver board, never wired straight to an Arduino pin

key_specs.gear_ratio: approximately 64:1 (63.68:1 exact ratio, widely cited across sources)
key_specs.stride_angle: 5.625 degrees / 64 (the motor's internal step before gearing)
key_specs.holding_torque: 0.03 N*m (0.3 kgf*cm / 300 gf*cm); this figure was independently confirmed by two separate sources (components101 and Botland)
key_specs.coil_resistance: 50 ohm per coil, per Botland's listing

visual_identification.shape_and_size: small round metal-cased can motor about 28 mm in diameter and roughly 19 mm deep, with a white plastic gearbox cap and a thin output shaft
visual_identification.color_and_markings: blue-grey or silver metal body; a white 5-wire pigtail (orange, pink, yellow, blue, red) exits one side ending in a small white 5-pin connector; '28BYJ-48' is often printed or stamped on a label on the can
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: '28BYJ-48' on a label or stamped on the metal can; sometimes a voltage rating like '5V DC' printed nearby
easily_confused_with: similar-looking 24BYJ or 35BYJ can motors used in HVAC dampers (different pinout/voltage)
a plain 2-wire DC gear motor (this part always has 5 wires, not 2)

example_connections.uno_pin: not connected directly to the UNO; the 5-pin motor connector plugs only into the ULN2003 driver board's motor socket
UNO digital pins 7, 6, 5, 4 respectively, per the DigiKey wiring example used for the driver board record

required_extra_parts: ULN2003 driver board (this motor cannot be safely driven directly from Arduino pins)
external 5V supply recommended for full torque
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: Stepper.h (built into the Arduino IDE) or AccelStepper (third-party)

hazards: very low voltage, no shock hazard
the internal gearbox can be damaged by forcing the shaft to turn by hand while powered, or by stalling it against a hard stop for a long time
handling_notes: don't force or over-tighten anything onto the thin 5mm output shaft
the 5-pin connector is keyed and only seats correctly one way into the driver board's socket
common_mistakes: trying to power the motor directly from an Arduino pin instead of through the driver board (it draws far more current than a pin can safely supply)
mixing up full-step and half-step code and expecting 4096 steps per revolution while running full-step mode (which only gives 2048)

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: motor buzzes or vibrates without turning
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: one of the 4 coil wires is loose or swapped, or the code's step sequence doesn't match the wiring
symptoms_and_causes.check: reseat the connector fully and verify the library's step table matches the coil wire order

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: motor turns the opposite direction from what's expected
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: the coil order is effectively reversed relative to what the code assumes
symptoms_and_causes.check: flip the sign of the step count in code rather than rewiring the connector

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: motor stalls or skips steps under light load
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: the driver board is being powered from the Arduino's onboard 5V regulator, which can't supply enough current under load
symptoms_and_causes.check: power the driver board's '+' pin from a separate 5V supply and confirm current draw with a multimeter in series

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the motor disconnected from the driver board, measure resistance between the Red wire and each of Orange/Pink/Yellow/Blue in turn; each should read roughly 50 ohm (per the coil resistance spec) and be close to equal across all four. An infinite (open) reading on any pair indicates a broken coil wire.

confidence.notes: ELEGOO's own tutorial and wiki pages for this motor could not be reached (403/404 errors during research), so identity and specs come from components101, a DigiKey maker tutorial, and the Botland retailer listing instead. Botland's price was listed in EUR (2.90 EUR / 2.44 EUR excl. tax) and converted to approximately 3.16 USD at an approximate rate that was not independently fetched in this session; treat this price as approximate.
